body.p: Applicant respectfully requests reconsideration of the present application in view of the foregoing amendments and the reasons that follow.
Claim 1 has been amended. No new matter has been added. These amendments are made without prejudice or disclaimer.
Support for the amendment can be found, for example, in the Specification in paragraph [0055] and in FIGS. 3B-4.

After amending the claims as set forth above, claims 1-12 and 21-28 remain pending in this application with claims 10-12 being withdrawn from consideration. Applicant respectfully requests reconsideration of these claims.
Applicant's representatives held an interview with Examiner Pruitt and Supervisory

Examiner Lee on April 3, 2024, and a follow-up interview with Supervisor Lee on April 4, 2024. The interview summary received from the USPTO on April 5, 2024, generally summarizes the topics discussed during the interviews. Applicant appreciates the courtesies extended to Applicant's representatives by Examiner Pruitt and Supervisory Examiner Lee during the interviews.
The Advisory Action maintains the rejection of claim 1 under 35 U.S.C. § 102 in view of Katz. However, Katz does not anticipate the subject matter of claim 1 because Katz does not

satisfy the requirement that "a prior art reference must disclose all elements of the claim within the four corners of the document, and it must disclose those elements arranged as in the claim." See Microsoft Corp. v. Biscotti, Inc., 878 F.3d 1052, 1068 (Fed. Cir. 2017).
The Advisory Action indicates that the actuator of Katz does not "preclude[] the second end from being freely rotatable about the pivot axis." Specifically, the Office Action alleges:

The second end of Katz freely rotates with arm 25 about pivot axis 26 (fig 8) as claimed. It is free to rotate about the pivot axis because the actuator does not have to be used to hold the mass in the neutral position, i.e. when the actuator is not actively being actuated to move the mass the mass would rotate to a non-neutral position without the help of springs (par 0026) or by centrifugal forces (par 0028). For these reasons, Katz discloses the claimed
invention.
Applicant respectfully disagrees. Paragraph [0026] of Katz discloses "The mass is

preferably held in a central, neutral position when the rotor blade is not vibrating. This can be achieved, for example, with the help of springs or by appropriate control of the actuator," and paragraph [0028] of Katz discloses:

By aligning the lever arm parallel to the longitudinal axis of the rotor blade, the mass is automatically held in the neutral position by the acting centrifugal forces when the rotor blade is not vibrating. Additional springs
or a corresponding activation of the actuator is then not required for this.

Thus, Katz indicates that the mass is "held" in the neutral position by centrifugal forces, not that it is "freely rotatable" as recited in claim 1. That the centrifugal forces are sufficient to hold the mass in a single position does not suggest that the mass, which is coupled to an actuator, is "freely rotatable," nor does it suggest that "when the actuator is not actively being actuated to move the mass the mass would rotate to a non-neutral position without the help of springs," as alleged in the Advisory Action. Being "held in the neutral position" is not equivalent to rotating, nor does the Advisory Action establish any such equivalence. Thus, Katz does not disclose "within the four corners of the document" that "when the actuator is not actively being actuated to move the mass the mass would rotate to a non-neutral position without the help of springs," as alleged in the Office Action. Instead, Katz simply discloses that the lever arm may be "held in

the neutral position 14 by the centrifugal forces as long as the actuator 5 is not actuated." Because Katz does not disclose all elements of claim 1, arranged as in the claim, Katz does not anticipate claim 1.

Further, to the extent the Office Action speculates about how the "mass would rotate" if the actuator is "not actively being actuated," such conjecture cannot sustain an anticipation rejection. A reference relied on to prove anticipation "must be so clear and explicit that those skilled in the art will have no difficulty in ascertaining its meaning." See Ex Parte Ouellette, Appeal No. 2007-0807, 2008 Pat. App. LEXIS 5201 (B.P.A.I. 2008) (citing In Re Turlay, 304 F.2d 893, 899 (C.C.P.A. 1962)).
Nevertheless, in an effort to advance prosecution, claim 1 has been amended to recite

"when the base is attached to the rotor blade, the pendulum mass structure is coupled to the rotor blade only via the first end." As shown in FIG. 8 of Katz, the lever arm 25 is connected to an integral joint 26 at one end and to an actuator 5 at the other end. Thus, Katz does not disclose "a second end configured to rotate freely about the pivot axis in accordance with a rotational speed of the rotor blade about the rotor axis, wherein when the base is attached to the rotor blade, the pendulum mass structure is coupled to the rotor blade only via a freely rotatable connection at the first end," as recited in amended claim 1.

For at least these reasons, claim 1 is allowable over Katz. Claims 2, 3, 5, and 6 depend from claim 1 and are allowable for at least the same reasons as claim 1, even without regard to the further patentable features recited therein. Applicant respectfully requests withdrawal of the rejections under 35 U.S.C. § 102.
Claims 1-3 and 5-6 were rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 102(a)(1) as allegedly being anticipated by EP 2357356 ("Katz").
As discussed above, claim 1 recites that the pendulum mass structure includes "a second end configured to rotate freely about the pivot axis in accordance with a rotational speed of the

rotor blade." Katz does not teach this feature, at least because the "end proximate the mass 6" of Katz, which the Office Action equates to the second end of the pendulum mass structure, is coupled to an actuator 5 that "causes the mass [6] to move." (Katz [0013]). Paragraph [0014] of Katz further discloses that the "actuator is preferably designed as an electrically, pneumatically or hydraulically operating actuator." Thus, the mass 6 does not "rotate freely about the pivot axis" but rotates only upon actuation of the actuator 5, "which drives the mass [6] directly." (Katz para. [0056]). Accordingly, Katz does not teach or suggest, much less identically disclose, that a second end of a pendulum mass is configured to "rotate freely about the pivot axis in accordance with a rotational speed of the rotor blade," as recited in claim 1.

For at least these reasons, claim 1 is allowable over Katz. Claims 2, 3, 5, and 6 depend from claim 1 and are allowable for at least the same reasons as claim 1, even without regard to the further patentable features recited therein. Applicant respectfully requests withdrawal of the rejections under 35 U.S.C. § 102.

In the Final Office Action, Claims 7-9 and 28 were rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as allegedly being unpatentable over Katz. As discussed above, claim 1 is allowable over Katz. Claims 7-9 and 28 depend from claim 1 and are allowable for at least the same reasons as claim 1, even without regard to the further patentable features recited therein.

Claim 4 was rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as allegedly being unpatentable over Katz in view of U.S. Patent No. 5,639,214 ("Guimbal"). Claims 21-25 were rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as allegedly being unpatentable over Katz in view of U.S. Patent No. 2,426,130 ("Wald").

Claims 4 and 21-28 depend from claim 1. Guimbal and Wald do not remedy the deficiencies of Katz discussed above with respect to claim 1. Accordingly, claim 1 and its dependent claims, claims 4 and 21-28, are allowable over Katz, Guimbal, and Wald in any combination.
Applicant appreciates the indication that claims 26-27 are allowable.

To the extent a requirement for restriction and/or election of species was made final in this application, Applicant asserts that all pending claims other than those identified as withdrawn, are either generic or read on the elected invention and/or species. Applicant intends for this Reply to be fully responsive to the outstanding Office Action.
Applicant believes that the application is in condition for allowance. Favorable
reconsideration is respectfully requested. The Examiner is invited to contact the undersigned by telephone if it is felt that a telephone interview would advance prosecution.
Respectfully submitted,
